title: Pennsylvania Gives Its Agencies 60 Days to List Who Can Be Sent to a Disaster - NewsBreak
text:
16 hours ago Pennsylvania disaster response has $40 million behind it for state agency costs, double the $20 million that was available before the current budget, and the state now has a deadline to work out what that money can actually move. Gov. Josh Shapiro signed an eight-page order on Tuesday. It gives the state emergency management agency 60 days to list the staff, equipment and other assets it could pull in when a disaster outruns the people already working it. Every agency under the governor’s control then gets 75 days from receiving that list to say what it can hand over. Read full article
